title: Numerical Optimization, Second Edition: back matter with Appendix A (Background Material), Appendix B (A Regularization Procedure), references and index (Springer free preview)
contribution: Back matter of the 2006 textbook, joint voice of Nocedal and Wright. Appendix A gives the linear-algebra, floating-point, conditioning and analysis background, including Q- and R-rates. Appendix B gives an inertia-correction procedure credited to Wachter-Biegler, with constants called arbitrary and a hedge that its heuristics may not be adequate safeguards. The 322 references include 17 Nocedal entries (Byrd on 8; four cited as OTC reports later published) and 8 by S. J. Wright, and neither Dai 2002 nor Mascarenhas 2004. The preview is the uncorrected first printing: all nine Appendix A errata of B003 still stand. Dating and framing only.
problem_entry: Background the book assumes: real finite-dimensional spaces only ('In this book we work exclusively with vectors and matrices whose components are real numbers', p. 1); Hilbert-space details omitted (p. 5); double precision as the default arithmetic (p. 17). The B001 preface says the appendix was rearranged for stand-alone use (B001 p. 22).
key_idea: A.1 (pp. 1-20): norms, subspaces, eigenvalues and SVD, trace and determinant 'used in the analysis of Chapter 6' (p. 9); LU, Cholesky and QR with their flop counts and null-space uses (pp. 9-13); Bunch-Parlett, Bunch-Kaufman and bounded Bunch-Kaufman pivoting compared on cost and stability, with Bunch-Kaufman unsuitable for modified Cholesky (pp. 13-15); Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury and interlacing (pp. 15-16); floating point and cancellation (pp. 16-18); conditioning versus stability, with Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting 'stable for all practical purposes' despite worst-case growth of about 2^(n-1) (pp. 19-20). A.2 (pp. 20-37): sequences; Q- and R-rates, with an R-linear sequence whose error rises every second step (pp. 22-23); topology and convex sets; Lipschitz continuity; derivatives, directional derivatives on the l1 norm; mean value, integral and implicit function theorems; order notation; scalar Newton and secant steps. Appendix B (pp. 38-39): Algorithm B.1 (inertia correction for (19.25)). Factor with delta = gamma = 0; on zero eigenvalues set gamma = 1e-8*eta*mu^beta; start delta at 1e-4, or at delta_old/2; multiply delta by 10 until the inertia is (n+m, l+m, 0). Adapted from Wachter and Biegler [301], with a stated rationale: large modifications erase second-derivative information and give steepest-descent-like steps.
assumptions: Real finite-dimensional spaces (pp. 1, 5); IEEE double precision, unit roundoff about 1.1e-16 (p. 17); Frechet differentiability (p. 28); Lipschitz Jacobian for the 0.5*L*||p||^2 linearization bound (p. 33). Informal steps are flagged: a proof 'left as an exercise' (p. 31), '(Prove this statement!)' (p. 22).
proof_devices: Textbook-standard background only, listed for scope. Cauchy-Schwarz via the discriminant of a quadratic in alpha (pp. 3-4).
Product of Lipschitz functions bounded by 2ML||x0 - x1||, (A.43) (p. 28).
Linearization error 0.5*L*||p||^2 from the integral form (A.57) and (A.12) (p. 33).
R-linear sequence (A.35) as a counterexample to monotone error decrease (p. 23).
experiments: n/a. Appendix B gives 'typical choices' of constants, not experiments (p. 39).
positioning: 322 references (pp. 40-55), the latest dated 2005-2006 (e.g. [301], 2006, p. 54). Nocedal is an author of 17 (my count), mapped to corpus IDs: [46] S011 (as OTC TR 18, 2005), [47] S042 (as OTC 2004/07), [48] S009, [49] S035, [50] S008, [52] S014, [53] S020 (pp. 42-43); [123] S012 (p. 46); [143] S021 (p. 47); [191] S027 (as OTC report, 2004), [194] S002 (p. 49); [200] S040, [209] S030 (p. 50); [228] S007, [229] S019 (p. 51); [303] S013 (as OTC 2003-6, p. 54); [322] S005 (p. 55). Byrd co-authors 8 of them, Waltz 4. S. J. Wright is an author of 8: [84], [121], [217], [315]-[319] (pp. 44, 46, 50, 54). There is no joint Nocedal-Wright paper. Not cited: Dai 2002 and Mascarenhas 2004 (the only Dai entry is [85], Dai-Yuan 1999 on CG, p. 44); S061 (Byrd-Marazzi-Nocedal), although Wachter-Biegler's failure example is [299] (p. 54); the 1995 L-BFGS-B paper S003; Frank E. Curtis ([83] is A. Curtis 1974).
writing: Definitional prose with small worked examples (Examples A.1 and A.2, pp. 30, 32). Practical verdicts set against the worst case ('for all practical purposes', p. 20). Explicit hedges on heuristics: 'All constants used in the algorithm are arbitrary' (p. 39). The index wording is the book's own: the BFGS method has the sub-entry 'self-correction, 142' (p. 57); 'Noise in function evaluation, 221-222' (p. 62).
limits_future: Scope, inferred from the index set against the B001 chapter ranges: complexity indexed only on pages of the linear-programming chapters 13-14 (pp. 57, 64, 66); noise only at book pp. 221-222, at the start of the new derivative-free Chapter 9 (pp. 59, 62); stochastic optimization only at book p. 7 (p. 66); KNITRO's own entry at book pp. 490, 525, 583, 592 (p. 60), one of 18 codes under Software (p. 66). What those pages say is not read. Errata check: B003 items 72-80 (book pp. 600-629) are all uncorrected in this preview (pp. 3, 5, 12, 18, 19, 20, 21, 23, 32). With the printing line '987654321' (B001 p. 5) this points to the first printing; the printing rule is stated for the first edition (B011 p. 3), so applying it here is my inference. Slips not in B003: 'A is m × m orthogonal' for Q (p. 12); 'α1s2 + α2s2' (pp. 5-6); words missing in 'Different norms can by the use of a subscript' (p. 5).

method_links.note: Framing only, in the joint voice of Nocedal and Wright; do not count it in Method 5's say-do tally. The appendix makes the rate of convergence one of the key measures of an algorithm's performance (p. 22). It judges partial pivoting by observed rather than worst-case growth ('stable for all practical purposes', p. 20). Complexity is indexed only for linear programming (pp. 57, 64, 66; inferred). Exclusivity fails against Wright's taste marks 1 and 4. Also consistent with the Method 5 limitation and C1: neither BFGS counterexample (Dai 2002, Mascarenhas 2004) is in the 2006 bibliography (pp. 40-55; the only Dai entry is [85], p. 44), which answers the 05 section 3.1 question at the bibliography level. Also on the card, with no entry: taste mark 8 and Heuristic 5, variant but not attributable, since Appendix B's numbers, called 'arbitrary' (p. 39), belong to Wächter and Biegler's procedure [301] (08 section 13.7: checked, not linked).
Weak: the joint textbook indexes 'self-correction' under the BFGS method (p. 57; book p. 142 not read). Joint voice of Nocedal and S. J. Wright; framing only.

Dating nuance, not a contradiction, to the anatomy's 27 years in which noise was set aside: the joint 2006 textbook indexes noise in function evaluation (p. 62) and finite differencing and noise (p. 59) inside the new Chapter 9, so the claim holds for his research papers only (SKILL.md now says so, C21). The body pages 221-222 were not read.
Dating, for the constant 'the Byrd partnership': Byrd co-authors 8 of the 17 Nocedal entries the textbook cites (pp. 42-43, 55; card's count). The reference list is a joint choice.

transferable: Give every factorization or pivoting rule its flop count and its stability, and say which downstream use it is unsuitable for (pp. 10-15).
Present a parameter procedure as heuristic, with typical constants and a stated limit (p. 39).
Date a co-authored text through its bibliography: count each author's entries and mark which are cited as reports (pp. 42-55).
Before quoting a preview, test the published errata for its pages against the text to identify the printing (pp. 3-32).
coauthors: Stephen J. Wright (co-author of the book; joint voice)

quotes.text: In practice, however, large growth factors are rarely observed, so we conclude that Algorithm A.1 is stable for all practical purposes.
We emphasize, however, that all of these are indeed heuristics and may not always provide adequate safeguards.

title: Review of Numerical Optimization (second edition, 2006) by Neculai Curteanu in zbMATH Open, Zbl 1104.65059
contribution: A signed, purely descriptive zbMATH review of the second edition, in the reviewer's voice, routed to peer critique (05). The reviewer names the two new chapters (9 DFO, 19 interior-point NLP), lists all chapters and the appendices, and the reorganizations and additions. That list follows the Preface to the Second Edition (B001 pp. 21-22) item by item. The review omits the preface's size remark, the typo-list promise and the list of uncovered areas, adds the OTC software-guide link, and contains no criticism.
problem_entry: The reviewer reviews the second edition against the first-edition review, which stays 'a reference point' (p. 1).
key_idea: In the reviewer's account (p. 1): new 'weights' for fields and topics; two new chapters, 9 (derivative-free) and 19 (interior-point methods for NLP); the full chapter list; (a)-(b) reorganizations (Newton distributed, large-scale in Ch. 7; common SQP/IPM material in Ch. 15, barrier methods moved to Ch. 19); (c)-(h) additions (duality, inequality QP, dual simplex and presolve, practical IPM-LP, CG for QP, filter and nonsmooth penalty methods); revised exercises, solutions manual, Perspectives and Software sections. Compared with B001 pp. 21-22: this agrees in content and order. The differences: the reviewer writes 'theoretical, algorithmic, and computational approaches' where the preface has 'the demands imposed by practical applications'; the reviewer omits the 'only slightly longer' remark, the web typo list, the acknowledgments and the areas not covered; the reviewer adds the software-guide link; 'derivation-free' and 'expended' are the reviewer's slips.
positioning: Anchored to the first-edition review (Zbl 0930.65067) and the Argonne OTC software guide; no other book cited (p. 1).
writing: Descriptive paraphrase of the preface plus the chapter list. The only evaluative phrases gloss the preface ('of great interest in applications', 'a basic domain in successful codes') (p. 1).
limits_future: Names no weakness, omission or error (p. 1). Confirms 05-peer-critique (Gaps, item 12) for the second edition: descriptive, no criticism.
transferable: When a review's list of changes mirrors the preface, treat it as a paraphrase and report only where the two differ (p. 1; B001 pp. 21-22).
coauthors: Neculai Curteanu (reviewer; not an author of the book)

quotes.text: Two new chapters are enclosed in this edition: Chapter 9 deals with derivation-free optimization, which is of great interest in applications, and Chapter 19 is devoted to interior-point methods for nonlinear programming, a basic domain in successful codes for nonlinear programming.
the review of the first edition remaining still as a reference point

title: Numerical Optimization: the authors' book web pages on Nocedal's Northwestern homepage (Internet Archive captures, 2002-2016)
contribution: The authors' joint third-person self-description of the book ('focusing on the methods that are best suited to practical problems'). It is identical on the first-edition page (captured 2002) and the second-edition page (2006), so it dates from the first edition. The pages also give errata links (Errata2 August 2006, Errata1 January 2000), at least three first-edition printings with corrections updated 2/12/06, and a second-edition HTML errata page still '[not yet posted]' in 2016, although the PDF list (B003) existed. Dating and framing only.
problem_entry: What the authors say the book is for: 'a comprehensive and up-to-date description of the most effective methods in continuous optimization', aimed at practical problems (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: The description on p. 1 (2002 capture) equals that on p. 2 (2006 capture), apart from layout. p. 2 links 'Errata2 (Second edition, August 2006)' and 'Errata1 (First edition, January 2000)'. p. 3: corrections to the first printing and to the 'second and third printings (updated 2/12/06)', with a rule to identify the printing from the last digit of the printing line. p. 4: 'Errata in the Second Edition [not yet posted]'. Link targets are not visible in the stripped HTML.
positioning: n/a; the pages point only to Springer and booksellers (pp. 1-2).
writing: Third-person self-description, the same on both captures: 'pleasant to read, informative, and rigorous', revealing 'both the beautiful nature of the discipline and its practical side' (pp. 1-2).
limits_future: Dating: the description existed by the 2002-06-01 capture (p. 1); the second-edition errata are dated August 2006 on the home page (p. 2); first-edition errata were updated into 2006 (p. 3). The HTML errata page for the second edition was never filled in, as late as the 2016 capture (p. 4), so the preface's typo-list promise (B001 p. 22) was kept through the PDF (B003), not through this page. Nothing about a third edition.

method_links.note: Joint framing: 'focusing on the methods that are best suited to practical problems' (pp. 1-2). The base tier already quotes this text (02 W1); the 2002 capture dates it to the first edition. Fails exclusivity against Wright's Method 2 and his taste mark 1, so it is shared framing, not Nocedal-specific.
Dating: errata for both editions, printings identified, updates into 2006 (pp. 2-3). Shared with Wright (his Heuristic 5, keep public errata). Joint.

transferable: Give readers a rule for identifying their printing, and keep one errata sheet per printing (p. 3).
Check a web errata page against the files it should link: here the HTML stub lagged the PDF list (p. 4; B003 p. 1).
coauthors: Stephen J. Wright (co-author of the book; joint voice; pages hosted by Nocedal)

quotes.text: It responds to the growing interest in optimization in engineering, science, and business by focusing on the methods that are best suited to practical problems.
Errata in the Second Edition [not yet posted]

title: Numerical Optimization: Springer catalogue pages for the first and second editions (About this book, Reviews excerpt, bibliographic data)
contribution: Springer's catalogue text for both editions, with the voices sorted. For the second edition, the first paragraph and the last sentence of the second paragraph repeat the authors' web page (B011), and the other sentences (graduate text, handbook, solutions manual) are not found in the authors' texts read. The first edition's 'About this book' is the first-edition Preface opening verbatim (B005 p. 6), including the exclusion of discrete and stochastic optimization. An MMOR 2001 reviewer's praise is quoted. Publication data: hardcover 27 July 2006, eBook 11 December 2006, XXII + 664 pages against XXI + 636.
problem_entry: The publisher's account of each edition (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: p. 1 (2nd ed.): first paragraph and last sentence of the second paragraph = B011 pp. 1-2 (verified); other sentences ('thoroughly updated throughout', new chapters 'used widely in practice', 'accessible to a wide audience', graduate text, handbook, solutions manual) not found in B011, B001 or B005: publisher's or unknown voice. p. 2 (1st ed.): 'About this book' = the first paragraph and the first sentence of the second paragraph of the first-edition Preface (B005 p. 6, checked), which resolves the a2-02 S010 card's open point. 'Reviews' excerpt: MMOR 2001, an unnamed reviewer (route to 05). The 'Editors' label on p. 2 versus 'Authors' on p. 1 is not meaningful (item note).
assumptions: Scope of the first edition, in the authors' preface words repeated by the publisher: discrete and stochastic optimization omitted (p. 2).
positioning: Affiliations: 1999 Nocedal at Northwestern ECE, Wright at Argonne MCS (p. 2); 2006 Nocedal at Northwestern EECS, Wright at Wisconsin CS (p. 1).
writing: Catalogue text. 'Quasi-Newton method' is the only named method among the keywords of both editions (pp. 1-2).
limits_future: Dating: 2nd ed. hardcover 27 July 2006, eBook 11 December 2006, softcover 1 April 2009, XXII + 664 pages (p. 1); 1st ed. XXI + 636 pages, eBook 6 June 2006 (p. 2). That is 28 more numbered pages (my arithmetic), consistent with the preface's 'only slightly longer than the first' (B001 p. 22). Framing (my inference): the 1999 textbook excludes stochastic optimization, and Nocedal's research turned to sampled and stochastic methods from 2009/10 (SKILL.md Research Trajectory). This is joint scope, not method evidence.
transferable: Sort a catalogue blurb by voice: match each sentence against the authors' own texts before attributing it (p. 1; B011 pp. 1-2; B005 p. 6).
coauthors: Publisher text (Springer); the book is by Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright

quotes.text: Because of our focus on continuous problems, we have omitted discussion of important optimization topics such as discrete and stochastic optimization.
It also serves as a handbook for researchers and practitioners in the field.

title: Corrections to Numerical Optimization, Second Edition (last updated May 27, 2008): errata list from Nocedal's homepage
contribution: The authors' joint public self-correction of the 2006 textbook: 80 numbered items from book p. 5 to book p. 629, published August 2006 and last updated May 27, 2008. In my classification: 14 spelling or grammar fixes, 36 formula, symbol or index fixes, 24 changes of wording that alter a statement, 4 exercise statements, 1 replaced proof paragraph (book p. 325), and 1 removed paragraph citing Goldfarb [132] (book p. 63). Theory of constrained optimization (Ch. 12) has 18 items; the new interior-point chapter (Ch. 19), SQP (Ch. 18), CG (Ch. 5) and linear programming have none. It confirms SKILL.md Heuristic 7's '80 numbered book errata' at card level.
problem_entry: Publish after printing what was wrong, located by book page and signed line (pp. 1-5).
key_idea: Corrections, my classification. Spelling/grammar: items 1, 2, 9, 17, 19, 32, 38, 39, 48, 51, 58, 61, 66, 67. Formulas/symbols/indices/constants: items 3-6, 10, 11, 15, 16, 20, 23, 24, 26, 28-30, 33-35, 40, 43-45, 55-57, 59, 63-65, 68, 74, 76-80 (e.g. 'half the Lipschitz', book p. 81; the integrand should be Hessians, book p. 167; 'at most 1/2' -> 'at most 3/4', book p. 279). Statement-changing wording: items 7, 8, 13, 14, 18, 22, 27, 31, 36, 37, 46, 47, 49, 50, 52, 54, 60, 62, 69-73, 75 (e.g. 'will be able' -> 'will not be able', book p. 40; 'closed convex set' -> 'closed set', book p. 315; '⇒' -> '⇔', book p. 341; positive definite -> semidefinite, book p. 468). Exercises: items 21, 25, 41, 42 (Ex. 10.5 adds the hypothesis that grad r_j is bounded). Proof replaced: item 53 (book p. 325). Paragraph removed: item 12 (book p. 63; [132] = Goldfarb 1980 on negative-curvature curvilinear paths, B002 p. 47; its content not read). Per chapter, mapped by me through the B001 TOC (pp. 7-16): Ch1 2, Ch2 3, Ch3 7, Ch4 9, Ch6 4, Ch7 4, Ch9 8, Ch10 5, Ch11 5, Ch12 18, Ch15 2, Ch16 4, App. A 9; none in Ch5, 8, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19 or App. B.
proof_devices: The only proof repair (item 53) makes z 'an implicit function of t' and derives z'(0) = d from the implicit function theorem, closing part (ii) (p. 4).
positioning: Credits three readers: Carlos Henao, Jorgen Sand, Marc Steinbach (p. 5).
writing: Terse numbered items located by page and signed line; replacements given in full (items 11, 53, 75); one self-explaining parenthesis (item 26) (pp. 1-5). Formula items are garbled in the text layer.
limits_future: Dating: 'Published August 2006', '(Last updated May 27, 2008)' (p. 1). Corrections ran for 21 months after publication; no later update is visible (the 2017 capture is byte-identical, per the item note; the HTML page was a stub in 2016, B011 p. 4). Item 12 is the one item Wright's copy B004 (May 17, 2008) lacks, per the note. The list is incomplete: three Appendix A slips are unlisted (B002 card). Its nine Appendix A items are uncorrected in the Springer preview (B002 pp. 3-32).

method_links.note: 80 numbered, located corrections with credited finders, updated for 21 months after publication (pp. 1, 5). Fails exclusivity: the errata are joint, Wright keeps his own copy (B004), and Wright's Heuristic 5 is the same practice. Shared, not Nocedal-specific.
After publication: corrections published and dated, with one passage withdrawn rather than patched (item 12, p. 1). Joint.

transferable: Number errata, locate each by page and signed line, and give a replacement text for anything longer than a phrase (pp. 1-5).
When a passage cannot be repaired by a phrase, remove it and say so (item 12, p. 1).
Credit the readers who found the errors (p. 5).
coauthors: Stephen J. Wright (co-author of the book; joint voice)
